newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore dollar slips on late stop-loss sales.
newsitem.headline: Singapore dollar slips on late stop-loss sales.

text.p: The Singapore dollar succumbed to stop-loss sales in late trade on Wednesday and dealers said the currency could head lower in the near term.
"The market is rather short dollars. We've seen Europeans and Americans buying (dollar/Sing) today," a European bank dealer said.
She said stop-loss sales were triggered above the 1.4450 level, taking the Singapore dollar to a low of 1.4465 against the U.S. dollar, compared with its opening around 1.4430/35.
The domestic currency was quoted at 1.4458/68 at 0927 GMT.
The dealer said there could be further stops around the 1.4480/85 level. If that were broken, the Singapore dollar could drop all the way down to 1.4530.
The last time the currency approached that level was on March 26, when it fell to an 18-month low of 1.4528 on concerns about a diplomatic row between Singapore and Malaysia.

Dealers said Singapore authorities were now likely to accept such weakness in the currency in view of the U.S. dollar's steep rise against the mark and the decline in Southeast Asian currencies in recent weeks.
"The Singapore dollar cannot afford to be so strong with the rest of its trading partners coming off," a U.S. bank dealer said.
